Keywords: product 3d, bottle, can, device, packshot, glb, hero model, rotate product
Use When: The visitor's decision depends on the object's form and the product is the brand
Asset Spec: Single GLB, Draco or Meshopt compressed, under 40k triangles, one PBR material, textures 1024px max, Y-up, origin at base centre, real-world scale in metres
Libraries: three, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei (useGLTF, Environment, Center), meshopt or draco decoder
Implementation: Dynamic-import the Canvas component. useGLTF.preload only after the hero paints. Wrap in Suspense with the poster as fallback. dpr={[1, 2]}, frameloop='demand' with invalidate on interaction
Fallback: Poster PNG/WebP rendered from the same camera and lighting at the exact final composition, served at the same aspect ratio
Budget: GLB under 800KB compressed, 3D JS chunk under 350KB gzip, excluded from initial route weight, first frame within 2s on a throttled 4G profile
Checks: Network panel shows no three.js in the initial chunk; poster visible before the model; no CLS when the canvas mounts; GPU idle when the section is offscreen
Anti-pattern: Putting the Canvas at the root of App so three.js loads on every page including the ones with no 3D

Keywords: scroll 3d, model scrub, exploded view, assembly, rotate on scroll, storytelling
Use When: A sequence must be understood in order and each step maps to a scroll position
Asset Spec: Same as product-hero-glb plus named nodes for every animated part, or a baked glTF animation clip
Implementation: Drive object rotation/position through refs inside a ScrollTrigger onUpdate and call invalidate(). Never route scroll progress through React state
Fallback: Static image sequence of 3-5 key frames as a normal figure list with captions describing each step
Budget: Same as product-hero-glb; scrub must hold 60fps on a mid-range phone or drop to the image sequence
Checks: Frame timing under scroll; keyboard users can reach every step's information in text; pinned section not clipped at 360px
Anti-pattern: Re-rendering the React tree on every scroll frame by calling setState from onUpdate

Keywords: configurator, variants, colourways, customise, material swap, options
Use When: The visitor genuinely chooses between options that change what they receive
Asset Spec: One GLB with swappable materials or morph targets; never one GLB per variant when only colour changes
Implementation: Preload only the default variant. Swap material colour/map on selection. Keep the selection in URL state so a configuration is shareable
Fallback: Static images of each variant in a normal radio-group gallery with the same labels
Budget: Base GLB under 1MB; each additional texture set under 200KB; variant switch under 150ms
Checks: Selection state announced; variants distinguishable without colour vision; URL restores the configuration; texture memory does not grow per switch
Anti-pattern: Loading every variant texture up front so the first paint pays for options nobody selects

Keywords: gradient mesh, shader background, ambient, noise, aurora, blob, atmosphere
Use When: Rarely. Only when a flat CSS gradient genuinely cannot express the identity
Asset Spec: No model. A single full-screen quad with a fragment shader; no textures
Libraries: three or ogl, or a 2D canvas alternative
Implementation: Single plane, no post-processing, capped DPR at 1.5, pause via IntersectionObserver, pause on document.hidden
Fallback: CSS gradient or a static WebP of one shader frame — visually near-identical at a fraction of the cost
Budget: Under 60KB JS; must not appear in the initial chunk; zero GPU work when offscreen
Checks: Battery and GPU profile with the tab backgrounded; contrast of overlaid text against the animated extremes
Anti-pattern: Shipping 500KB of three.js to render a moving gradient that a 12KB CSS animation would have matched

Keywords: model-viewer, web component, ar, quick look, simple 3d, no framework
Use When: A single model needs viewing and possibly AR without a custom scene
Asset Spec: GLB plus USDZ when iOS AR is required; both from the same source asset
Implementation: Lazy-load the script with loading='lazy' and a poster attribute. Set camera-controls, ar, and a descriptive alt
Fallback: The poster attribute is the built-in fallback; also provide the product photograph in the page
Budget: Component script under 150KB gzip lazy-loaded; GLB under 800KB
Checks: AR entry works on a real device or is hidden; poster shown before interaction; alt text describes the object
Anti-pattern: Using model-viewer for a scene that needs custom lighting and materials, then fighting the component

Keywords: 360, panorama, virtual tour, equirectangular, room view, walkthrough
Use When: A space must be judged before a visit and photographs cannot convey the volume
Asset Spec: Equirectangular JPEG/WebP, 4096x2048 maximum, progressive, one per viewpoint
Libraries: three sphere mesh with BackSide material, or a panorama web component
Implementation: Load the low-resolution version first and swap to full resolution after interaction. Provide viewpoint navigation as buttons not only hotspots in the sphere
Fallback: A normal photo gallery of the same space with captions per viewpoint
Budget: Each panorama under 600KB at full resolution; low-res preview under 60KB
Checks: Drag and arrow-key navigation both work; viewpoint labels are text; no motion sickness trigger from auto-rotation under reduced motion
Anti-pattern: Auto-rotating panoramas that start moving without a user gesture

Keywords: 3d text, extruded type, geometric hero, abstract shapes, brutalist 3d
Use When: Only when the typography itself is the product (type foundry, studio identity)
Asset Spec: Geometry generated in code; no external model. Fonts converted to typeface JSON only if extrusion is essential
Implementation: Generate geometry once and memoise. Prefer drei Text (SDF) over Text3D for readable copy
Fallback: The same words as real HTML text styled with CSS — which is also what search engines and screen readers need
Budget: Under 200KB JS; the words must exist in the DOM as text regardless
Checks: The headline text is present in view-source; contrast measured on the rendered result; no reliance on the canvas for meaning
Anti-pattern: Rendering the h1 only inside WebGL, making the page's main claim invisible to crawlers and assistive technology

Keywords: particles, points, dust, stars, confetti, field
Use When: Almost never on a microsite. Only when the particles encode real data or brand-critical material
Implementation: Cap at 5000 points on mobile and 20000 on desktop. Single draw call, additive blending off unless needed, no per-frame allocation
Fallback: Static noise texture or nothing at all
Budget: Under 80KB JS; frame budget under 4ms on a mid-range phone
Checks: Frame timing with the CPU throttled 4x; battery drain over 60 seconds; disabled entirely under reduced motion
Anti-pattern: Allocating a new Float32Array inside the render loop, producing garbage-collection stutter every few seconds

Keywords: poster, placeholder, loading strategy, progressive, suspense, lazy canvas
Use When: Every WebGL section — this is the required wrapper for all patterns above
Asset Spec: Poster image at the canvas aspect ratio in WebP with a PNG fallback, rendered from the actual scene
Implementation: Render the poster as a normal img with width/height attributes. Observe the section; on first intersection dynamic-import the canvas and cross-fade once loaded. Keep the poster mounted until the first frame renders
Fallback: The poster is the fallback: it stays if WebGL is unsupported, if the import fails, if reduced motion is set, or if deviceMemory is under 4
Budget: Zero 3D bytes until intersection; no CLS at swap because both share the same box
Checks: Throttled 4G first-paint check; DevTools WebGL disabled; prefers-reduced-motion set; import forced to fail
Anti-pattern: Rendering a spinner instead of a poster, so the section is a blank box during the entire model download

Keywords: webgl detect, fallback detection, save-data, device memory, capability, feature detect
Use When: Every WebGL section — decides whether the 3D mounts at all
Implementation: const ok = (() => { try { return !!document.createElement('canvas').getContext('webgl2'); } catch { return false; } })(); const lean = navigator.connection?.saveData || (navigator.deviceMemory ?? 8) < 4 || matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches; mount3D = ok && !lean;
Fallback: Poster path taken whenever the gate returns false
Budget: Zero cost; runs before any 3D import
Checks: Verify each branch by forcing it: disable WebGL, emulate Save-Data, set deviceMemory, enable reduced motion
Anti-pattern: Assuming WebGL availability and catching the failure with a try/catch that leaves an empty container
